dialogues.speaker: Paricia
dialogues.text: The ocean is like a giant sapphire gem.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It should sell for a good price.

dialogues.speaker: Paricia
dialogues.text: Ah, I bet it'd go for a fortune.

dialogues.speaker: Paricia
dialogues.text: Moreover, different regions of the ocean have different shapes and colors. If we could cut the gem by the directions of the current, or even flip those directions around...

dialogues.speaker: Paricia
dialogues.text: Ah, my apologies. My thoughts just kind of took off on their own. It's hard to get out of the mindset of a gemstone merchant.

dialogues.speaker: Paricia
dialogues.text: I love gemstones just as much as I love the sea. It's pretty difficult to strike a balance between the two.

dialogues.speaker: Paricia
dialogues.text: Thankfully, I've got a regular business partner here, so I can come over here as often as I want.

dialogues.speaker: Paricia
dialogues.text: Transaction volume has been pretty good lately, but it hasn't involved money.

dialogues.speaker: Paricia
dialogues.text: As you know, the land of the Children of Echoes is rich in gemstones but somewhat lacks other resources.

dialogues.speaker: Paricia
dialogues.text: I've been using the connections I've built up through business to trade gemstones, weapons, and tools for a lot of useful supplies for the tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Paricia
dialogues.text: In terms of being able to gaze out to sea without care, sorting out all of this has been even more effective than making a huge profit.
